## Packet wire

Constants, enums, flags and types: bit-packed structs exchanged between client and server with exactly the same protocol version.

A cell is ✅ when the language's packet leg passes on this branch: the examples generated and run against the shared wire vectors the C++ reference writes (make test-<lang>), with the packet-text (#519) and packet-defaults (#396) gates and their negative controls.

## Fixed Tables

Fixed tables provide versioning such that a new reader can always read an old writer. They are good for messages between the game server and a backend, or the backend and the website where the reader and writer have different versions of the protocol.

This work is on main: sprint/schema-vt-core landed on main, and the Go core (sprint/schema-go) lands through dev (2026-10-21). Cells show ✅ verified complete or ❌ not yet verified complete: a cell is ✅ only when every task under it is done with its acceptance recorded, by the landed cards, in docs/roadmap-evidence/. Built, partial and unstarted states stay in the source data; the [feature survey](docs/FIXED-TABLES-SURVEY.md) records the full scope.

## Variable tables

Variable tables are the table wire's variable class: pointers and the flat node table, maps, unbounded arrays, blobs, union arms of any field type, retain-unknown, the text, block, cook and message forms, and the reflection that walks them. C++ is the reference; C, C# and Go carry the whole class.

Rust, Java, JavaScript, Dart and Elixir carry the card constructs (the subset the sprint's card record uses) and refuse the rest by name. A cell is ✅ only when the whole row is carried and its tests pass on this branch, so a card-constructs-only port stays ❌ until the rest of the row lands; each ❌ cell's source data says what exists and what is missing.

A leg that is red at the branch head holds its cells ❌ even where the row's tests exist: the source data names the one task that holds them, so one fix card turns them green together.

Schema is built by Glenn Fiedler, together with AI collaborators that do much of the building, testing and porting. Glenn owns every design decision. Every month a [public ledger](https://github.com/mas-bandwidth/patreon#public-ledgers) shows where the AI collaborator's tokens went, by repository, and what they bought.
